  // Adapted from Emscripten's DYNAMIC_EXECUTION=0 invoker, with this build's
  // optional-argument check and synchronous-only behavior preserved.
  function craftInvokerFunction(humanName, argTypes, classType, cppInvokerFunc, cppTargetFunc, isAsync) {
    if (argTypes.length < 2) {
      throwBindingError("argTypes array size mismatch! Must at least get return value and 'this' types!");
    }
    assert(!isAsync, 'Async bindings are only supported with JSPI.');
    var isClassMethodFunc = argTypes[1] !== null && classType !== null;
    var needsDestructorStack = usesDestructorStack(argTypes);
    var returns = argTypes[0].name !== 'void';
    var expectedArgCount = argTypes.length - 2;
    var minArgs = getRequiredArgCount(argTypes);
    var invokerFn = function(...args) {
      checkArgCount(args.length, minArgs, expectedArgCount, humanName, throwBindingError);
      // Per-call storage also supports a JS callback reentering the same binding.
      var destructors = needsDestructorStack ? [] : null;
      var argsWired = new Array(expectedArgCount);
      var invokerFuncArgs = [cppTargetFunc];
      var thisWired;
      if (isClassMethodFunc) {
        thisWired = argTypes[1].toWireType(destructors, this);
        invokerFuncArgs.push(thisWired);
      }
      for (var i = 0; i < expectedArgCount; ++i) {
        argsWired[i] = argTypes[i + 2].toWireType(destructors, args[i]);
        invokerFuncArgs.push(argsWired[i]);
      }
      var rv = cppInvokerFunc(...invokerFuncArgs);
      if (needsDestructorStack) {
        runDestructors(destructors);
      } else {
        for (var i = isClassMethodFunc ? 1 : 2; i < argTypes.length; ++i) {
          var param = i === 1 ? thisWired : argsWired[i - 2];
          if (argTypes[i].destructorFunction !== null) {
            argTypes[i].destructorFunction(param);
          }
        }
      }
      if (returns) return argTypes[0].fromWireType(rv);
    };
    return createNamedFunction(humanName, invokerFn);
  }
